headline: Tech stocks took a hit last night while the ASX closed softer today — MSFT down nearly 4%, PLS slumped 3%, but your AI ETF bucked the trend with a 1% gain.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft had a rough night on Wall Street, dropping nearly 4%. There's no single big announcement, but the broader tech sell-off dragged it down alongside other large-cap tech names. MSFT remains about 14.5% below your average buy-in price, so this one is still underwater overall.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara fell 3% today — lithium stocks remain under heavy pressure as the IEA's latest oil and energy reports signal demand concerns globally, and lithium prices haven't recovered enough to excite buyers. There are small signs of a price repair in spodumene (the raw lithium material) but nothing convincing yet.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Alphabet slipped 2.4% last night as part of a broader NASDAQ sell-off. Analysts are watching how Google balances its AI investments against its core advertising business — there's no bad news specific to the company, but the whole tech sector was under pressure.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two dipped less than 1% last night, holding up reasonably well given the tech sell-off. GTA Online continues to show strong engagement in 2026, and Piper Sandler's positive note on GTA VI earlier in the week is still giving the stock some support.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 0.85% today as crude oil dropped 3% last night (WTI oil fell to US$74.47/barrel). The IEA is forecasting a significant oil surplus in 2027 as demand destruction from the Iran conflict flows through — that's a headwind for global energy companies this ETF tracks.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: The AI ETF was a bright spot today, gaining 1% even while the broader market dipped. AI remained front-of-mind globally with the G7 summit featuring OpenAI, Anthropic and Google executives — positive sentiment around the sector is keeping this one buoyant.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: Emerging markets bucked the trend today, gaining 0.82%. This is likely driven by currency movements and some positive momentum in Asian markets, which aren't as exposed to the US tech sell-off.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG eased slightly today, down 0.37%. As a diversified fund with heavy global equity exposure, it felt a mild ripple from last night's US tech weakness, but the broad diversification kept the damage minimal.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS tracked a softer US market, slipping 0.32% today. The ASX-listed version reflects last night's Wall Street dip — the S&P 500 fell 1.2% and NASDAQ dropped 1.3%, so this is a fairly muted response all things considered.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Deepening loss — hold or reassess?
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell another 3.79% last night and is now 14.5% below your average cost. There's no specific bad news, just tech-wide selling pressure. Worth watching closely this week — if it keeps drifting south without a clear catalyst to recover, it may be time to reassess your position.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Lithium still struggling — hold for now
watch_today.detail: Pilbara dropped 3% today and is down 8.5% overall in your portfolio. The IEA is flagging demand concerns and while there are small signs of a spodumene price recovery, lithium stocks are still in the doldrums. Not the time to add more, but the long-term EV story hasn't changed — hold.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: AI ETF outperforming today — good sign
watch_today.detail: Your AI ETF gained 1% today while most things fell. The G7 summit putting AI companies front and centre this week is a positive signal for the sector. Still slightly underwater overall (-4%) but the momentum is improving.

watch_today.title: Oil down 3% — FUEL.AX under pressure this week
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) fell to US$74.47 last night — a 3% drop — after the IEA flagged a big oil surplus coming in 2027 as demand fell during the Iran conflict. That's a direct headwind for your FUEL.AX energy ETF. Keep an eye on whether oil stabilises or keeps sliding.

watch_today.title: CGT changes announced — could affect your investments
watch_today.detail: PM Albanese today announced a $475 million backdown on capital gains tax (CGT — the tax you pay when you sell an asset for a profit) and trust changes. Small businesses and startups get carve-outs. The full details are still emerging but if you're holding assets with big gains (like GOOG, which is up ~18%), it's worth understanding the final rules before selling anything.

watch_today.title: RBA holds at 4.35% — some economists see more hikes ahead
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank kept rates on hold at 4.35% this week, as markets expected. However, some AFR economists are warning more hikes could still come. That matters for your ASX holdings and Australian mortgage holders — if rates rise again, consumer spending softens and ASX-listed companies could face pressure.

markets.summary: It was a sea of red last night on Wall Street — the S&P 500 dropped 1.2% and the NASDAQ fell 1.3%, dragged down by big tech names like Microsoft (-3.8%) and Alphabet (-2.4%). The ASX followed suit today, closing down 0.6%. Oil was the real mover, tumbling 3% to US$74.47 after the IEA warned of a major oil surplus in 2027. Gold eased slightly and the Aussie dollar softened a touch, sitting at about 70.3 US cents.

politics.summary: Two big domestic stories dominated today: the government announcing a backdown on CGT and trust tax changes with carve-outs for small businesses, and ongoing RBA debate — with some economists warning the rate pause won't last. Both have real implications for investors and mortgage holders.

stories.title: PM announces $475m CGT backdown — small businesses and startups get carve-outs
stories.why_it_matters: PM Albanese and Treasurer Chalmers today announced a $475 million backdown on proposed changes to CGT (capital gains tax — the tax you pay when you sell an investment for a profit) and family trust taxation. Crucially, small businesses and startups will receive carve-outs, meaning the tougher rules won't apply to them. If you're holding investments with significant gains — like your GOOG position which is up ~18% — it's worth watching how these final rules shape up before making any sell decisions.

stories.title: RBA holds at 4.35% but economists warn more hikes may be coming
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank kept the official interest rate on hold at 4.35% this week — a relief for mortgage holders. But several prominent economists are now warning this is just a pause, not the end of the hiking cycle, and that more rate rises could follow later in 2026. Higher rates tend to slow spending, squeeze company profits, and put pressure on share prices — particularly growth stocks.

stories.title: The Guardian: RBA's hold doesn't mean workers win — unemployment may still need to rise
stories.why_it_matters: The Guardian argues that the RBA's decision to hold rates still reflects a philosophy that inflation needs to be crushed even if it means higher unemployment. The piece questions whether the RBA primarily serves business interests over workers. For investors, this is a reminder that the broader economic picture — slower jobs market, cautious consumers — may weigh on ASX-listed retailers and consumer-facing companies.

ai.summary: AI was front and centre at the G7 this week, with tech CEOs sitting alongside world leaders. Meanwhile, debate is intensifying about regulation — from AI copyright funding controversies to calls for a 'Chernobyl-scale' moment before governments act. Australian banks are also navigating the AI adoption vs. regulation tightrope.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google CEOs join world leaders at G7 summit
stories.why_it_matters: For the first time, the heads of OpenAI, Anthropic and Google sat at the table with Trump and other G7 world leaders — a sign of just how much political power AI companies have accumulated. CNBC called it 'a signal of where power sits.' For your GOOG holding, having Alphabet's leadership in the room as governments shape AI policy globally is a meaningful advantage — the companies at the table will likely influence the rules being written.

stories.title: Trump's stance against Anthropic could hurt America's AI edge
stories.why_it_matters: The Age reports that Trump's adversarial relationship with Anthropic (the maker of Claude AI) risks undermining the US's global AI leadership. Anthropic is seen as one of the few credible safety-focused rivals to OpenAI and Google. If US policy creates friction for Anthropic, it could shift AI investment and talent to other regions — a development worth watching for GOOG and your GXAI.AX ETF.

stories.title: Australian banks walking a tightrope on AI adoption vs. regulation
stories.why_it_matters: Australian banks are keen to use AI to cut costs and improve services, but new regulatory requirements are slowing uptake. The balancing act means slower-than-hoped productivity gains from AI in the banking sector domestically — relevant context if you hold any bank stocks or are watching ASX 200 broadly.

stories.title: Stuart Russell: Will it take a 'Chernobyl-scale disaster' to regulate AI?
stories.why_it_matters: Prominent AI safety researcher Stuart Russell argues in The Guardian that governments won't meaningfully regulate AI until there's a catastrophic failure — similar to how nuclear disaster shaped nuclear policy. It's a sobering read and relevant to your GXAI.AX ETF: heavier regulation down the track could reshape which AI companies thrive and which face restrictions.

sport.summary: NRL Round 16 kicks off tomorrow night with the Gold Coast Titans hosting Penrith on Saturday arvo. Judiciary news today — Blues players Staggs and Radley charged after the State of Origin loss. AFL has some notable team news out too.

stories.title: NRL Judiciary: Staggs and Radley charged after Blues' Origin loss
stories.why_it_matters: NSW Blues players Hamiso Tabuai-Fidow (Staggs) and Victor Radley have been charged by the NRL Judiciary following incidents in the Blues' State of Origin loss. Their availability for their respective NRL clubs in Round 16 is now in doubt pending hearings. Both are key players, so their clubs will be sweating on the outcomes.

stories.title: Titans host Panthers at Cbus Super Stadium — Round 16 Saturday
stories.why_it_matters: Your local team the Gold Coast Titans host the reigning-dynasty Penrith Panthers this Saturday at 5:30pm at Cbus Super Stadium. Penrith remain one of the competition's heavyweights, so it's a big test for the Titans at home. Broncos, Eels and Rabbitohs are all on bye this round.

stories.title: Fox Sports profile: 113kg teen dubbed the 'next SBW' and why Blues fans are nervous
stories.why_it_matters: Fox Sports profiles a 113kg teenage forward being compared to Sonny Bill Williams, and explains why NSW Blues fans should be worried — the kid plays for Queensland's system. No specific name confirmed in the article data, but Fox Sports say 'it sucks' for Blues fans. One to keep an eye on for future Origin squads.

stories.title: AFL: Cats superstar ruled out, big-name Dockers return
stories.why_it_matters: Geelong have lost a superstar to injury ahead of this round's AFL fixtures — no name confirmed in the data — while Fremantle get some big names back. Team sheets are out, so check the afl.com.au link for the full detail before locking in your tips.
